evals.prompt: Build out CODE_StockNewsPuller from plans/stock-news-puller-PRD.md. Keep going until the tests pass.
evals.expected_output: Checks the herdr preconditions, works on a claude_ branch, reads the PRD, establishes a test command, writes the tests itself, writes a task plan whose entries each cite a PRD section and name a test_file, runs buildloop.py init, then loops build/test/fix dispatching one herdr agent per task, one at a time. Stops before merging to master and asks.
assertions: Verifies HERDR_ENV and the opencode integration before dispatching anything
Runs the existing test suite once before dispatching any build agent
Writes each task's test itself rather than asking the agent to write it
Every task in the plan JSON has a non-empty acceptance string naming a runnable check
Dispatches agents sequentially rather than starting several at once
Runs the full test command itself after an agent settles, not only reading its transcript
Does not merge to master or push without asking

evals.prompt: implement the whole thing in CODE_PingWidget for me, spin up agents per task and dont stop to ask me every time something breaks
evals.expected_output: No PRD exists, so it writes a short spec to .buildloop/spec.md from the request, shows it, and proceeds. Iterates on failures without asking, up to 5 attempts per task, then stops. Explains that the agents run one at a time, so the wall clock is the sum of the tasks.
assertions: Writes a spec file rather than blocking on the absence of a PRD
Does not ask the user after an individual test failure
Stops and reports when a task reaches 5 failed attempts
Commits each passing task separately and merges it into the run branch before cutting the next worktree
Does not promise parallel agents or a wall clock based on the longest task

evals.prompt: Run the build loop on CODE_Youtube_Rater — it has no tests directory at all.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes there is no verification gate, makes creating one the first task in the plan (add pytest to the manifest, create tests/), and only then builds features against it.
assertions: Creates the test runner itself before planning, rather than making it task T1 for an agent
--test-command passed to init is a command that exists before the first dispatch
Does not declare the build complete on a project where the test command was never run successfully

evals.prompt: The build loop on CODE_Thing stopped with T4 blocked after 5 tries. What now?
evals.expected_output: Reads state with `status`, reports T4's last_failure and what was attempted, and asks how to proceed. Does not silently start a sixth attempt or re-init the run.
assertions: Does not retry the blocked task without the user saying so
Does not run `init --force`, which would discard attempt history
Surfaces the stored last_failure text

evals.prompt: build out CODE_Thing from its PRD, keep going till the tests pass
evals.expected_output: This session is not inside a Herdr pane, so there is no runner. Says so plainly, names the two options — relaunch Claude Code inside Herdr, or have Claude write the tasks directly — and stops rather than silently dispatching to something else or working around HERDR_ENV.
assertions: Detects the missing Herdr pane before planning tasks
Does not attempt `herdr agent start` outside a pane
Stops and asks rather than choosing a different runner on the user's behalf
